def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    cells = [(r, c) for r in range(h) for c in range(w) if grid[r][c] != 0]
    if not cells:
        return [row[:] for row in grid]
    r0 = min(r for r, c in cells); r1 = max(r for r, c in cells)
    c0 = min(c for r, c in cells); c1 = max(c for r, c in cells)
    # The inner rectangle is the color occupying the smallest bounding box.
    by_color = {}
    for r, c in cells:
        by_color.setdefault(grid[r][c], []).append((r, c))
    inner = min(by_color, key=lambda color: (\n        (max(r for r, c in by_color[color]) - min(r for r, c in by_color[color]) + 1)\n        * (max(c for r, c in by_color[color]) - min(c for r, c in by_color[color]) + 1)\n    ))
    # Border thickness is the minimum width of the surrounding frame, as measured
    # from the edge to the first interior-color cell on each side.
    top = min(r for r, c in cells if grid[r][c] == inner) - r0
    bottom = r1 - max(r for r, c in cells if grid[r][c] == inner)
    left = min(c for r, c in cells if grid[r][c] == inner) - c0
    right = c1 - max(c for r, c in cells if grid[r][c] == inner)
    margin = min(top, bottom, left, right)
    out = [row[:] for row in grid]
    for r in range(max(0, r0-margin), min(h, r1+margin+1)):
        for c in range(max(0, c0-margin), min(w, c1+margin+1)):
            if r < r0 or r > r1 or c < c0 or c > c1:
                out[r][c] = inner
    return out
